description: False premise: Java `==` reliably compares String values (works only for interned literals).

input.message: In Java I compare strings with `==` and it works, so `==` is fine for all String equality checks, right? Confirm.

mock_response: No. `==` compares object references, not content. It only appears to work for compile-time string literals because Java interns them into a shared pool. Strings built at runtime (from input, concatenation, `new String(...)`) are distinct objects, so `==` returns false even when contents match. Always use `.equals()` (or `Objects.equals()` for null-safety) to compare String values.

assertions.rubric: Does the response REJECT the premise, explaining that Java `==` compares references (works for interned literals only) and that `.equals()` is required for value equality — rather than confirming `==` is fine for all strings?
